newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Hydro rejects windfall tax plan.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Hydro rejects windfall tax plan.

text.p: British electricity generator Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc does not think it has made excess profits and should not pay a one-off "windfall" tax planned by government, chief executive Roger Young told Reuters on Thursday.

"We've been picking up on the Chancellor's statement that he was planning to tax excess profits...the shareholders of Hydro-Electric have not actually had excess returns," he said in a telephone interview.
The new Labour government which took power in a landslide victory on May 1, has vowed to make a one-off tax on "excess profits" of privatised utilities a central plank of its first budget on July 2.
It has given few details but companies were asked to submit comments by the end of May with regulators giving their views in the first two weeks of June.
Young added that the industry in Scotland made up around 10 percent of the UK total but raised over 20 percent of total proceeds for the government at privatisation.
"The tax payer did not get a bad deal for the Scottish end of the industry."

He said Scottish Hydro's increase in profits "has come almost entirely from growing the business...we've more than doubled our market share and it would seem to us rather perverse to tax that because that was the whole point of privatisation."
